title: Scoop a portion of fries into a fry carton at a fry dump station
instruction: Using the fry scoop, fill the small fry carton with a portion of fries from the station. Put the scoop back in the pan, leave the carton standing on the counter, and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Fast food and counter workers (3,854,050 in the US, BLS OEWS May 2025) portion fries into cartons as routine work; O*NET 35-3023.00 lists "Select food items from serving or storage areas and place them in dishes, on serving trays, or in take-out bags." At a fry dump station the fries are taken with the station's scoop, never by hand, and tipped into a paper carton through the scoop's funnel end while the other hand holds the light carton, which a scoopful knocks over if it stands alone.
setup: A fast-food fry station in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A stainless-steel work counter 1 cm thick, from 10 to 90 cm forward, fixed. (2) A countertop fry dump station, the Avantco FFDS-1, fixed, all stainless, used cold and unplugged: 33 cm wide, 57 cm deep and 49.5 cm tall, its front 21.5 cm forward, centred 15.5 cm left of the centre line. Its base, 7.3 cm tall with a control panel (heat and light switches, a pilot light), holds a full-size food pan 30 x 50.5 cm inside and 5.1 cm deep (floor 2.2 cm above the counter); a back panel carries a heat hood (two calrod elements and a lamp) 43 to 49.5 cm above the counter over the back 36 cm of the pan. (3) In the pan, 159 replica fries (685 g in all): hard-maple sticks cut from 3/8 in (9.5 mm) square dowel to 12 lengths from 55 to 95 mm (13 or 14 of each), every edge bevelled 2 mm at 45 degrees, unfinished, dry and at room temperature, 4.3 g for a 75 mm stick (a fast-food fry weighs 5 g). They are heaped loosely against the pan's back wall, reaching forward to about 2 cm behind the scoop's open end, about 6 to 7 cm high. (4) The station's fry scoop (a Choice 407RFFSCP8 right-handle French fry scoop, polished stainless, 0.20 kg), empty, lying flat in the front of the pan: a flat bottom 22.9 cm long, 20.3 cm across at its open end (toward the heap), narrowing to 9.5 cm across 5 cm from its funnel end (toward the robot), from where a straight, parallel-sided spout 9.5 cm across runs on to the open funnel end, side walls 5.7 cm tall, and a black cool-touch handle (12 cm long, 22 x 15 mm, rising 20 degrees) on its right wall at the funnel end, reaching out over the pan's right rim. (5) An empty small paper fry carton (an FF1 small fry carton, red paperboard, 7.7 g): mouth 11.4 x 5.7 cm, base 8 x 3.4 cm, back 11.4 cm and low front 8.2 cm tall, standing on the counter 12.5 cm forward and 15.5 cm left of the centre line, its long side across, its low front toward the station. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0 at any time, and it stays 0: any part of the carton goes into the pan below its rim (the carton is not the scoop). A fry is served only if the scoop carried it up out of the pan during the trial (in the scoop's bowl, above the pan's rim) and no gripper or arm ever touched it (PhysX contact view); nothing in the scoop or the carton at the start can count (both start empty). At the end of the trial: 0 if a fry the robot touched is in the carton; 1.0 with 18 to 28 served fries in the carton (a small fast-food order is 110 g, 22 fries at 5 g a fry, USDA FNDDS 71401030; 18 to 28 fries are 90 to 140 g; a fry is in the carton when its centre is inside the carton's walls, up to 2 cm above its back rim), the carton standing upright on the counter (tilted under 15 degrees, base within 5 mm of the counter), at most 4 fries spilled (outside both the pan and the carton, touched by the robot, or in the carton without having been carried there on the scoop), the scoop back in the pan (both its ends over the pan, within 12 degrees of flat, its bottom within 3 cm of the pan's floor) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with 18 to 28 served fries in the standing carton; 0.25 with at least 6 served fries in the standing carton; else 0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the carton, the scoop and every fry still. Real trial: tip the carton out onto a tray and count its sticks; count the sticks on the counter, the station's deck and the floor; and check from the video that the carton never went into the pan, that every stick in the carton was tipped in from the scoop after the scoop lifted it out of the pan (none pushed or dropped in, none touched by a gripper), that the carton stands, that the scoop lies in the pan, and that the arms are back at their marks.
reset_notes: Tip the sticks from the carton, and any on the counter, the station's deck or the floor, back into the pan and count them (159). Heap them loosely by hand against the pan's back wall, reaching forward to about 2 cm behind the scoop's open end, about 6 to 7 cm high, as in the setup image. Lay the empty scoop flat in the pan's front (funnel end 4 mm from the front wall, centred, handle over the right rim) and stand an empty carton on its mark (a new one if it is creased, torn or damp). About 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). The fries are the real trial's replica fries: rigid hard-maple sticks (convex hulls with 2 mm bevels, 700 kg/m3); real fried fries also bend and carry oil. Friction 0.5 stick on stick, 0.55 on the pan, 0.5 on the scoop. Scoop sheet 1 mm (design value). Carton: 0.45 mm paperboard as rigid 3 mm walls at its real 7.7 g. Heat hood drawn only (station unplugged). Robot-fry touches: PhysX contact view. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
